answer: Consider an agent marketplace where brokers earn fees moving cargo: timber lots, crystal ingots, and other inspected goods. To resist sybils, every broker must attach a proof of work over a real shipment manifest and its key; peers reject any manifest already used. One operator cannot mint a nebula of ghost brokers without shipping equally many real loads, since each identity needs a distinct audited manifest. Faking a hundred identities means moving a hundred real timber shipments or buying compute to forge hashes, and that cost exceeds what the ghosts collect, so sybil attacks stop paying.
